{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-pa-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"e0c77b7aec57fb90d3c536bc24692382e080d12b930562ad5c1979b243f88808","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-pa-class-c:lineage:65","source_registry_sha256":"643bc755bc144bbb64c82e5b21691c27918519b2f96f9b0ff96b63899c04fddb","source_liveness_sha256":"d125293461efac0b369397a252e58fe1686ca24cdc89a306e2ea205c1feddb7c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Laws restraints and related issues","heading":"C — Laws restraints and related issues","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Laws restraints and related issues

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
Notify PennDOT within fifteen days after a name or address change, including a move out of state. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
Pennsylvania does not issue driver-license products to nonresidents. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
Use Form DL-80 to request a non-commercial license name change, correction or replacement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
Carry the license update card with the driver license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A01
Drivers and front-seat passengers in cars, light trucks and motorhomes must wear seat belts. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A01
Passengers aged eight through seventeen must wear belts in every seating position. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A01
A driver under eighteen may not carry more passengers than the available seat belts can accommodate. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A01
During a crash, an unrestrained body continues moving after the vehicle stops. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A01
Belts spread rapid-deceleration force over the chest, hips and shoulders instead of hard vehicle surfaces. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A01
Wear a seat belt even when the vehicle has airbags. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A01
Belts help keep occupants inside the vehicle during a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A02
A child under two rides rear-facing until outgrowing the seat manufacturer's maximum height and weight limits. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A02
Never place a rear-facing child seat in front of an airbag. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A02
For required child seats or boosters under age eight, follow the vehicle and seat instructions to secure the seat tightly and the child snugly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A02
Never leave a child or pet alone inside a vehicle, even with partly open windows. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A02
Do not let children play in an unattended vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A02
Place a needed item in the rear seat or move a reminder toy forward when placing a child in the seat to avoid forgetting the child. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A02
Bulky winter coats can compress in a crash and leave excessive slack, so the child-seat harness must be snug against the body. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A02
Children under four require a federally approved child restraint secured by a seat belt or LATCH, regardless of seating position. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A02
Children from four to under eight require an approved booster secured using lap and shoulder belts wherever seated. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-F21 | anchor: A02
Children from eight to under eighteen require a belt wherever seated, and the driver is responsible for securing minors properly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-F22 | anchor: A03
Wear the lap belt snugly across the hips and the shoulder strap across the chest away from the neck. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec15-F23 | anchor: A03
Sit as far from the airbag as practical while maintaining access to pedals and controls, at least ten inches from the steering wheel. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec15-F24 | anchor: A03
Hold the wheel at nine and three or eight and four, with thumbs on the top or outer rim rather than inside. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec15-F25 | anchor: A03
The handbook recommends rear-seat travel for children twelve and younger. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec15-F26 | anchor: A03
Airbags are supplemental restraints, so lap and shoulder belts remain necessary. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec15-F27 | anchor: A03
PennDOT describes accessible testing centers and sign-language interpreter assistance for applicants with hearing impairments. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec15-F28 | anchor: A03
Applicants needing sign-language assistance should state their preferred form, such as ASL, PSE, SEE or oral interpretation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

Misconceptions: airbags supplement belts; a disability placard alone does not authorize parking without its beneficiary; safe bicycle passing has an explicit centerline exception.
Mnemonics: update the record, restrain every rider and protect the cyclist.
Glossary: LATCH is the vehicle child-seat attachment system; a booster works with lap and shoulder belts; the Dutch Reach uses the hand farther from the door.
